title: Products distributed through intermediaries
summary: The stream-of-commerce problem asks when a manufacturer’s distribution of a product through others supplies a sufficient connection to the state where litigation is brought. It is especially difficult when the manufacturer does not directly sell to the ultimate forum customer.
notes: The assigned opinions do not yield one unqualified formula accepted by all Justices. Record the narrower holding and the competing approaches instead of turning a plurality into a universal rule.

sections.Meaning: The stream-of-commerce problem asks when a manufacturer’s distribution of a product through others supplies a sufficient connection to the state where litigation is brought. It is especially difficult when the manufacturer does not directly sell to the ultimate forum customer.
sections.How to work through the question: Identify the intended distribution market, the defendant’s conduct, the intermediary’s role, and any evidence of forum-specific targeting. Compare Gray, World-Wide Volkswagen, Asahi, and Nicastro while distinguishing their facts and the votes supporting each rationale.
